items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: We had a very good little band, and Osie and I wrote some six-piece arrangements

ctx.x: Anyway, Osie was one of those people who was just an excellent musician. He worked with Earl Hines' band... Well, after our band, we had this... I don't want to get ahead of myself here. After the guys began to go into the Army, Osie Johnson, Leonard Phillips and a fellow named Harry Curtis, an alto player (Leonard Phillips, the trumpet player, Osie Johnson, the drummer), Tommy Potter (bass), and a young tenor saxophone player who was 18 then, and he was also at Armstrong High School, and his name was Charlie…

We had a very good little band, and Osie and I wrote some six-piece arrangements that all the musicians that came from around the country, and came to the Howard Theatre, and they would come down and hear us, and admire us for sounding like a big band. But at this time, Osie and I were experimenting with all kinds of arrangements. Sometimes on ballads behind
